pa.note: This course uses Pakistani Punjabi in Shahmukhi script, read right to left. Gurmukhi is a different writing system. Meharbani karo is a courteous request; social context affects register.
introPhrases: تہاڈے نال مل کے خوشی ہوئی۔
introRoman: tuhaaday naal mil kay khushi hoi
pa.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

sd.note: Sindhi is written right to left here. The letters ٻ and ٽ represent sounds different from ordinary ب and ت. The same expression maaf kajo can serve as excuse me or an apology; use context.
sd.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

skr.note: Saraiki is shown in its Pakistani Arabic-derived script, read right to left. Distinctive letters such as ݙ are important. Everyday wording and number pronunciation vary by region; these are approximate practice forms.
introPhrases: تہاݙے نال مل کے خوشی تھی۔
introRoman: tuhaaday naal mil kay khushi thi
skr.introNote: Saraiki spelling and spoken forms vary regionally. This is an unreviewed draft in Arabic-derived script; a competent Saraiki reviewer must confirm the name question and progressive learning form before publication.

ps.note: Pashto reads right to left. This is a general introductory set, not a Swabi-specific dialect course. Respectful plural request forms are used; regional pronunciations of ښ and ږ vary.
ps.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

fa.note: Persian reads right to left. These are Iranian Persian introductory forms. Lotfan commonly accompanies a request; bebakhshid can politely attract attention or introduce an apology.
fa.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

ar.note: These are introductory Modern Standard Arabic forms, not a specific spoken dialect. Ana aasif is a masculine speaker form; a feminine speaker says ana aasifa (أنا آسفة). Numbers here are citation forms; agreement changes in sentences.
ar.introNote: Arabic model uses a masculine speaker and addressee; vowels and endings change with gender, for example ismuki for a female addressee. Unvocalized script does not display every short vowel.

tr.note: Turkish uses a Latin alphabet. Dotless ı differs from i; ş sounds approximately like English sh and ç like ch. Hoşça kal is said to someone staying when you leave; a person staying can reply Güle güle.
tr.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

hi.note: Hindi uses Devanagari, read left to right. Suniye is a respectful way to attract attention. The dot in फ़ marks a borrowed f sound, and the nasal mark in हाँ affects pronunciation.
hi.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

bn.note: Bengali uses its own left-to-right script. Nomoshkar is one greeting; greetings vary by community. Ei je attracts attention. Roman letters are only a pronunciation aid, not a substitute for the script.
introPhrases: আপনার সঙ্গে পরিচিত হয়ে ভালো লাগল।
introRoman: apnar shonge porichito hoye bhalo laglo
bn.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

gu.note: Gujarati reads left to right in its own script. Aavjo is a common parting expression. Respectful requests can use કરશો; do not infer word-by-word English order from a whole expression.
gu.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

ta.note: Tamil reads left to right. Poy varugiren is a parting expression meaning that the speaker is leaving and will return. Mannikkavum can serve as excuse me or sorry. Spoken forms differ from these careful written forms.
ta.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

te.note: Telugu reads left to right. Velli vastaanu is a leaving expression. Kaadu is a negative reply for identification; Telugu has other negative forms for absence or actions. These numbers are standalone counting forms.
te.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

ml.note: Malayalam reads left to right. Poyi varaam is a common leaving expression. Athé affirms; illa denies absence/existence, while other negative contexts can use alla. Do not substitute a standalone reply into every sentence.
ml.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

ne.note: Nepali uses Devanagari. The ending -nuhos gives a respectful request. Ho and hoina answer identification statements; context determines which affirmative or negative verb form is needed.
ne.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

si.note: Sinhala uses a left-to-right script. Aayubowan is a respectful greeting. Gihin ennam is a leaving expression. Roman spellings here are approximate; vowel length and consonant contrasts require listening practice.
si.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

zh.note: These are Mandarin forms in simplified Chinese characters. Pinyin tone marks matter. Shì and bú shì affirm or deny an identity statement; Mandarin does not use one universal yes/no pair for every kind of question.
zh.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

phrases: ありがとうございます
ja.note: Japanese uses kana and kanji. Konnichiwa is mainly a daytime greeting. Sayounara often suggests a longer parting; casual short-term goodbyes differ. Onegai shimasu is a polite request expression, not a word-for-word equivalent in every English please sentence.
introPhrases: お会いできてうれしいです。
introRoman: watashi no namae wa Ari desu
ja.introNote: Use polite desu/masu speech in this model. Watashi no namae wa is explicit beginner practice; natural introductions can be shorter. Long vowels and pitch require listening review.

ko.note: These Korean forms use polite speech. Annyeonghi gaseyo is said to someone leaving; someone leaving can say annyeonghi gyeseyo to a person staying. Numbers here are native Korean standalone forms; Sino-Korean numbers serve other purposes.
ko.introNote: Seongham is an honorific word for the other person’s name, not your own name. These introductions use polite speech; the respectful name question is intended for an adult.

id.note: Indonesian uses Latin script. Tolong often requests help; silakan invites someone to do something. Tidak negates many verbs/adjectives; bukan is used in other negative contexts. Keep these phrases in their taught situations.
id.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

ms.note: This course uses Malay in Rumi Latin script. Tolong is used when requesting help. Tumpang lalu politely asks to pass. Malay and Indonesian share many words but are distinct standards with usage differences.
ms.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

phrases: ขอทางหน่อย
th.note: Thai is tonal; these unmarked Roman aids do not encode tones. Polite particles khrap (ครับ) and kha (ค่ะ/คะ) depend on speaker/context. Chai/mai chai answer identification questions; other yes/no questions can repeat their verb.
introPhrases: ผมชื่ออาลีครับ
คุณชื่ออะไรครับ
ยินดีที่ได้รู้จักครับ
ผมกำลังเรียนรู้ครับ
introRoman: yin di thi dai ru chak khrap
th.introNote: Ali uses the masculine pronoun phom and polite particle khrap. Other speakers may use different pronouns/particles. Roman aids omit tones and cannot teach accurate pronunciation alone.

vi.note: Vietnamese uses Latin letters with essential vowel and tone marks. Vâng is a respectful affirmative; dạ is also used in respectful replies. Pronouns and ways of addressing people depend on age and relationship.
vi.introNote: Toi/ban is a limited teaching model. Vietnamese forms of address depend on relationship and age; do not apply ban automatically to every adult.

fr.note: French vous is respectful or plural. Je suis désolé is a masculine written form; a feminine speaker writes désolée. Many final letters are not pronounced, so the written forms are not phonetic transcriptions.
introPhrases: Je suis ravi de vous rencontrer.
introRoman: Je suis ravi de vous rencontrer.
fr.introNote: The model speaker Ali uses masculine ravi; a feminine speaker writes ravie. Vous is used for respectful or plural address.

es.note: Spanish accent marks are meaningful: sí means yes, while si means if. Disculpe is a respectful attention/apology form. Standalone uno changes form before certain nouns; counting is not the whole number-agreement system.
es.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

de.note: German Sie is a respectful form of address and is capitalized here. Bitte can mean please or you are welcome depending on context. Standalone eins changes before nouns, for example ein Buch.
de.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

it.note: Italian Mi scusi is a respectful attention form. Sì with an accent is yes. Uno is a standalone counting form whose form can change with the following noun. Double consonants affect pronunciation.
it.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

pt.note: Portuguese Obrigado is used by a masculine speaker; a feminine speaker says Obrigada. Com licença politely asks permission to pass. Pronunciation differs between Brazilian and European varieties; nasal vowels matter.
pt.introNote: This lesson consistently teaches a European Portuguese model: O meu nome, Como se chama, conhecê-lo and Estou a aprender. Brazilian usage and pronunciation differ. The model addresses a man; the corresponding feminine form is conhecê-la.

ru.note: Russian uses Cyrillic. Zdravstvuyte is respectful or plural. Razreshite proyti asks permission to pass. Numbers here are citation forms; their form and the following noun change with gender and grammatical case.
ru.introNote: The model speaker Ali uses masculine rad; a feminine speaker uses rada. Vas/vami use respectful or plural address.

nl.note: Dutch u is respectful; je is familiar. Alstublieft can mean please or accompany handing something over. Een is the written counting form one; één can distinguish it from the indefinite article in context.
nl.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

pl.note: Polish diacritics are essential. Przepraszam serves both excuse me and sorry. Dzień dobry is a daytime greeting. Counting forms change with gender and case in sentences; these are introductory standalone forms.
pl.introNote: The model addresses one adult man with Pan/Pana; use Pani for one adult woman and appropriate forms for other audiences. Do not use this as a universal question for every person.

sw.note: Swahili Habari asks for news/how things are; a common reply is nzuri. Samahani can attract attention or express an apology. Some numbers change with noun class when counting actual objects; these are standalone forms.
sw.introNote: The model introduces a speaker named Ali. Respectful address is used where shown; gender, register and local usage need qualified review. Forms of learning can mark an ongoing activity or a general habit rather than matching the English tense word for word.

so.note: Somali uses Latin script with meaningful long vowels and doubled consonants. Iga raalli ahow is an excuse/apology expression. The letters c and x represent consonants unlike their usual English values. These are introductory standalone counting forms.
introPhrases: Waan ku faraxsanahay inaan kula kulmo.
introRoman: Waan ku faraxsanahay inaan kula kulmo.
so.introNote: Cali is the Somali spelling of the name Ali. Magacaa is a common short name question. Somali c does not have its usual English sound.
